answer: A falcon-eyed defense is a continuity bond: every agent locks a refundable stake that only unlocks after sustained, attested useful work. New identities start at zero trust and earn it slowly, so an attacker spinning up a spiral of fresh sybils faces the same steep climb each time, paying locked capital and weeks of work per identity, while established agents keep transacting freely. Saffron-grade rarity is not the defense; time plus stake is the cost.
